Platform metrics for CanadaLogin, in the `sre` schema. It holds two groups of
tables: incident tables, which record outages and how long they took to resolve,
and uptime tables, which record whether each monitored site was up and how fast
it responded.

The incident tables come from the CanadaLogin Platform team's
`CanadaLogin_MTTR_Dashboard` Google Sheet, maintained by hand in the CDS Google
Drive. The `sre-mttr-sheets-fetcher` Lambda reads it through the Google Sheets
API every Monday at 06:00 ET. Both tables have one row per incident and differ
only in history: `mttr_current` holds the latest state of each incident, while
`mttr_history` adds a dated snapshot of every incident on each upload.

:::

### Data quality

Because the source is a hand-maintained spreadsheet, a few caveats apply to both
tables:

- **Timestamps are strings, not native timestamps.** `detected_at`,
  `acknowledged_at`, `mitigated_at`, and `resolved_at` are text in America/Toronto
  local time at minute precision (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`). Parse them before doing date
  math. (`fetched_at` is a real timestamp, in UTC.)
- **URLs may carry trailing whitespace or embedded newlines.** Trim
  `slack_channel` and `postmortem_link` before joining on or rendering them.
- **Categorical columns are unvalidated free text.** `severity`, `service`,
  `component`, and `root_cause_category` are typed by hand, so expect occasional
  typos, casing, and spacing drift. The values listed in each field table are those
  observed so far, not a closed set.
- **The duration columns are rounded to the nearest minute** from second-precision
  source times, so recomputing them from the displayed (minute-precision) timestamp
  strings can differ by up to a minute.

## Uptime Tables

The uptime tables are sourced from the
[`cds-snc/status-statut`](https://github.com/cds-snc/status-statut) public
GitHub repository and updated automatically each day. No manual steps required.

::: {#uptime-tables}
:::
